title: The Neighborhood Association Model as a Mechanism for Participatory Governance and Economic Empowerment in Urban Communities
authors: Eny Boedi Orbawati, Fadlurrahman Fadlurrahman, Ari Mukti et al.
why: An Indonesian neighbourhood-association case that links participation to local economic empowerment. A comparison point for the neighbourhood work in the CDC course.
caveat: Qualitative and single-site. The empowerment claims are the authors' reading of participant accounts.
abstract: Community empowerment based on the Neighborhood Association (Rukun Tetangga / RT) model has demonstrated a positive impact on fostering self-reliance among urban populations, particularly through increased participation, communal solidarity, and the strengthening of local economies. This article specifically examines an empowerment model that prioritizes self-help mechanisms as its core strategy. The results reveal that direct engagement of residents at the RT level serves as a critical foundation for designing initiatives that align with the community’s actual needs. Active participation in program implementation further illustrates that RT-based empowerment effectively mobilizes communities in a cost-efficient manner. These results underscore the RT model as an innovative and contextually relevant approach to enhancing economic well-being through collective action. Therefore, the study recommends integrating RT-based empowerment into governmental policy as a sustainable strategy for urban community development.
